what_happened: The the person running Athena merged pull request 673 by hand on GitHub. This was the planner caller-list landing, job 20261116-004006-cvfn. Its checks had been green since 03:45 UTC, but the drain that was waiting to merge it ended before it did. With main behind the base, every later job ran its baseline checks locally, using about 13 GB each. Ten jobs were held for low disk before the the person running Athena stepped in.
cause: Merging a verified job's pull request depends on one drain staying alive to do it. Nothing else picks up a green, unmerged pull request after the drain ends. Nothing alerts anyone, and nothing links the unmerged state to the later jobs' cost. Without the merge, main stays behind the base, so later jobs lose the cheaper path and each rebuilds its baseline locally. That produces the disk holds.
other_causes: Each later job's baseline run is costly (about 13 GB) and the free-disk guard holds the job, so one stuck merge turns into many held jobs.
Nothing flags a landing that has been green but unmerged for hours (here from 03:45 to about 12:57 UTC).
open_hypotheses: Why the drain ended while waiting for the merge is not in the fields (crash, container reclaim, or a normal stop).
It is unconfirmed that main being behind the base is what forced the local baselines. The stated reason implies it.
The 10 held jobs may not all have been held for this reason.
prevention: Make merging a green, verified pull request a step that outlives any one drain. When a drain starts, and on a schedule, it should find pull requests that are green and unmerged and merge them through the normal land path, or raise a visible alert once one has waited longer than a set time. Before starting a job's baseline locally, Athena should also check for an unmerged green pull request that would bring main up to date, and report it. No gate's counts apply here, since every gate has 0 disagreements.
proposed_request: Make Athena merge green, verified pull requests even when the drain that was waiting on them has ended. At drain start, and on a recurring schedule, list the pull requests whose checks are green and which are still unmerged, and land each one through the normal `athena land` path. Do this oldest first, and do not bypass the history check. Make `athena status` show any pull request that has been green and unmerged for more than 30 minutes, with its age. Before a job runs its baseline locally because main is behind the base, check for such a pull request and put a warning in the job record. Acceptance: (1) a test drives a drain that ends with a green pull request unmerged, then starts a new drain, and shows the pull request lands; (2) a test shows status lists a pull request that has been green and unmerged for over 30 minutes; (3) a test shows the warning is recorded when the baseline runs locally while a green pull request is unmerged; (4) CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
